description:
FILED s473v (2026-09-16) from task #1803's profile tables.  PRE-EXISTING.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS.  sb-sprof :cpu, self time, on 2ac855aa:

  subste   (sb-pcl::fast-method cl-ppcre:scan (function t))   2.0 %
           (sb-pcl::emf cl-ppcre:scan)                        1.3 %
           sb-pcl::check-applicable-keywords                  2.2 %
           the two SYS:SRC;PCL;DLISP3.LISP lambdas            2.1 %
                                                       total  7.6 %
  textproc the same four frames, reached through cl-ppcre:split  7.7 %
           (cl-ppcre:split itself is 11.2 % total there)

That is exactly the cost task #680 removed for `m//`: it added %p-ppcre-scan,
which funcalls the scanner CLOSURE directly and skips the generic function's
effective-method lookup, its &rest consing and its keyword checking.

WHY s/// AND split DID NOT GET IT.  PCL does not drive those loops.
`do-regex-subst` hands the scanner to `cl-ppcre:regex-replace-all` (or
`cl-ppcre:regex-replace`), and `p-split` hands it to `cl-ppcre:split`; both of
those are cl-ppcre's own functions and they call `cl-ppcre:scan` the generic
way, on every match.  So the dispatch is inside a library function PCL calls,
not in PCL's own code, and no amount of shaping around the call reaches it.

THE THREE SHAPES A FIX COULD TAKE, none of them measured yet:
 1. Drive the replace loop HERE, the way the scalar m//g iterator already
    does: PCL already has %p-global-scanner (it wraps the scanner to give
    perl's advance rule, task #1719) and %p-write-match-target, so the missing
    piece is the result-string build and the count.  That also removes
    cl-ppcre's build-replacement (1.7 % self / 41.8 % total on subste â most
    of which is the engine underneath it, but not all).
 2. Shadow `cl-ppcre:scan`'s (function t) method, VERSION-PINNED with a loud
    refusal at load if its lambda list is not what the runtime expects â the
    #1461 pattern for `create-bmh-matcher`.  Cheapest, and it fixes `split`
    and every other cl-ppcre entry point at once.
 3. Nothing: it is 7-8 % of two rows, and the #71 engine question (USER-parked
    2026-09-07) would delete the whole call path.

MEASURE FIRST, whichever is chosen: the four frames are a SHARE of a row, and
a hand A/B of shape 2 on an isolated scan is minutes of work
(scratch/s473v/ab-lisp.pl in the s473v worktree is the tool).

NOT THIS ROUND: round 33's bar was 20 % of a row per lever and the three that
shipped (#1804, #1809, #1810) were 30-150 %.


================================================================
=== MEASURED AND NOT BUILT (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus) â the share is REAL and
=== SMALLER than it was, and it is under the round's bar ===

Re-measured on main 4c6565e5 with sb-sprof :cpu over each row's own emission
(scratch/s473x/prof.pl in the s473x worktree):

  subste   (N=40 000, 2 598 samples) â the generic dispatch of cl-ppcre:scan
           (sb-pcl::fast-method cl-ppcre:scan (function t))   3.0 % self
           (sb-pcl::emf cl-ppcre:scan)                        2.7 %
           sb-pcl::check-applicable-keywords                  3.3 %
           the SYS:SRC;PCL;DLISP3.LISP dispatch lambda        2.6 %
                                                       total 11.6 % SELF

  textproc (N=1 500, 4 952 samples) â the SAME four frames, reached through
           cl-ppcre:split (0.7 self / 14.3 total)
           fast-method 0.6, emf 0.4, check-applicable-keywords 0.6,
           two DLISP3 lambdas 1.0 + 0.6                total  3.2 % SELF

s473v measured 7.7 % on textproc.  The row has since gained #1804's match
record and #1461's BMH matcher, so the dispatch is a SMALLER SLICE OF A FASTER
ROW â the profile table going stale in the direction that matters (the s473v
rule).

VERDICT: this round's bar is 20 % of a row per lever.  11.6 % and 3.2 % are
under it, and the absolute prize over both rows is ~0.06 s.  NOT BUILT.
Reopen it when (a) a row's share crosses 20 %, or (b) something else in
`do-regex-subst` is being opened anyway â see the next paragraph.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE SUM: #1751 sits in the same code.  `do-regex-subst`'s
non-/e arm sets the match variables from an UP-FRONT scan it makes BEFORE the
replace loop, which is one extra scan per substitution AND leaves `$1`/`@-`/
`@+`/prematch/postmatch on the FIRST match where perl leaves the LAST.  If
shape 1 (drive the replace loop in PCL, on %p-global-scanner +
%p-write-match-target) is ever taken, recording the match by OVERWRITING one
record removes that scan and closes #1751 in the same change, and the two
prizes add.  Shape 2 (the pinned `scan` shadow) must NOT touch the record path:
it would leave #1751 open and unrelated.

ALSO VISIBLE IN THE subste PROFILE, and not this task's: cl-ppcre's
`build-replacement` is 2.7 % self / 22.3 % total, and the string-output-stream
it builds through is another ~14 % self (string-sout 4.3,
get-output-stream-string 2.9 + 1.9, %write-string 2.0, write-string 2.0,
%init-string-output-stream 1.2).  That is the result-string construction shape 1
would also replace, and it is bigger than the dispatch this task is about.
subject: cl-ppcre's OWN `scan` is called GENERICALLY by regex-replace-all and split â the CLOS dispatch %p-ppcre-scan removed for m// (#680) is still 7.6 % of subste and 7.7 % of textproc
